meta.description:
This outline covers mandatory briefing items required by the Air Force and McEntire Joint National Guard Base safety and health programs.  It does not cover required training for participation in specialized safety programs such as confined space, hazardous energy control (lockout/tag out), ladder safety, ALARA, and others.  Such training must be provided by the supervisor or through formal training. Training items for confined space, hazardous energy control and hazard communication in this outline cover general awareness training for all employees or describe how more in depth training will be provided.  For additional examples of specialized safety programs see the table at TAB 14.1.3. Job Specific Items in this notebook. 
Supervisors are required to review this job safety training guide annually and update whenever there is a change in equipment, procedures, processes or safety, fire protection, and health requirements.   Provide this briefing prior to the employees beginning work, or whenever there is a change in equipment, procedures, hazards or the work environment.

14.1.2.4. Requirements for reporting unsafe equipment, conditions or procedures to supervisor immediately. Procedures must include notification to employees that reporting unsafe conditions or work related injury or illnesses can be reported without fear of retaliation. (T-0)

	14.1.2.4.1. Purpose and location of AF Form 457, USAF Hazard Report. (T-1)
	
	14.1.2.4.2. Purpose and means to access the ASAP process. (T-1)
Supervisors brief reporting unsafe equipment, conditions, or procedures 
 
You should immediately report ALL unsafe equipment, conditions and/or procedures in your work area to your supervisor.  If you see something that’s unsafe don’t  overlook it and hope someone else sees it and fixes it.  Get involved!  If you can correct the hazard, do so, and then inform your supervisor of the situation.  Remember  SAFETY is EVERYONE’S responsibility!
 
IMMINENT DANGER and KNOCK IT OFF!! 

IMMINENT DANGER-is any hazard or procedure that poses immediate risk to life or limb of any person in the work place.  Any employee at McEntire JNGB that feels an  imminent danger situation exists or could develop is REQUIRED to call “KNOCK IT OFF!!” assertively and persistently.  At that point the supervisor or lead worker on the  scene will take the following steps: 
	1. Bring the work to a halt as safely and quickly as possible. 
	2. Identify the perceived hazard with the help of the work crew.  
	3. Discuss the safeguards that need to be implemented to accomplish the task. 
	4. Determine the new course of action and make sure all employees understand the new procedures. 
	5. Resume the task. 
 
It is the individual’s responsibility to report any unsafe equipment, condition, or procedure to the supervisor! 


Note:  Only qualified employees will perform maintenance on damaged equipment.  Damaged equipment will be identified with the appropriate tag, and locked out and tagged out if  applicable.
WHAT TO REPORT
 
WHO TO REPORT TO / INTERIM CORRECTIONS
 
a.  Equipment:
	Use of Danger Tags
 
 
All unserviceable equipment shall be tagged and removed from service.  If the item cannot be located where it will not present a safety hazard the item will be tagged with an appropriate tag.  (see below).
 
 
b.  Conditions or Procedures:
 
If you discover a condition or procedure that poses a safety hazard to yourself or others, notify the supervisor of the area immediately.  If you cannot find the supervisor, notify the next person in their chain of command until someone is notified. Notify your Unit Safety Representative, There are also several means to identify safety hazards and suggest corrective actions such as AFTO Form 22 and AF Form 1000 programs.  Elevate concerns up both the management and safety levels if you are not satisfied that corrective action removed the unsafe condition.
 

c.  Reporting Unsafe Equipment or Conditions:
 
Contact the area supervisor.  Always try to resolve problems at the lowest possible level.  If you are not satisfied with the supervisor’s action complete an AF Form 457, USAF Hazard Report and give it to the Wing Safety Personnel.
The AF Form 457s are located on each Safety Bulletin Board
 
Detecting unsafe or unhealthful working conditions at the earliest possible time and correcting hazards promptly at the lowest possible working level are essential elements of the AFOSH program.  The hazard-reporting program provides a system of reporting hazardous conditions and for investigating and correcting those hazards.  Any person assigned, attached, or under contract to the Air Force may report a hazard. Submit a hazard report (HR) on any event or condition that affects flight, ground, weapons, or space safety.  Reportable hazards include unsafe procedures, practices, or conditions.  AFI 91-202, USAF Mishap Prevention Program explains the hazard-reporting program in detail.
 
Hazard Reporting Procedures:
· 
 Report hazards to the responsible supervisor or local agency.  If the hazard is eliminated on the spot, no further action is required unless it applies to other similar operations or to other units or agencies.
									 
· If the hazard presents imminent danger, the supervisor or individual responsible for that area must take immediate action to correct the situation or apply interim control measures.
									 
· Report hazards that can't be corrected at lower levels to the safety office via AF Form 457, USAF Hazard Report, or by telephone or in person.  You may submit reports anonymously.

· An Important Note on Hazard Reporting: Supervisors must ensure blank AF Form 457 is kept readily available to workers and workers know where the forms are located.  Workers should never have to “ask” for the forms.  They should be readily available so a worker can grab it and submit it anonymously if they choose.  Federal Law prohibits reprisal to any employee who submits a hazard report or reports a hazardous condition.
